title: The First Wave
text: “This is a little different from human magic, isn’t it? Anything goes, really… you.”
“Preparations are more or less done, nyoink! Now then, Older Sister! Please look after the village’s defenses, I say!”
“Yes, yes… I’ll leave this side to you lot, and um… I’ll take care of the feudal lord.”
“Understood, nyoink!”
Apparently, if Éclair’s parents died, it would trigger — and accelerate — the slave hunts. So I’d left the task of protecting Big Sister’s parents and buying time in this village to Older Sister.
“If it gets too dangerous for Big Sister to handle alone, just give a shout.”
“Will do, nyoink!”
Knowing exactly how far to push things was proving quite the delicate balancing act, I must say. And so, I was about to face a wave unlike any I had experienced in all my previous loops.
Older Sister carried Keel’s parent on her back and returned to the village. There, she explained that she’d found them collapsed by the roadside, gathering the villagers around her.
Then, the countdown to the next wave hit zero. With a sharp crack echoing through the air and a violent gust of wind, I too was transported to the wave’s location.

Whoooosh! A particularly strong wind. A wave-like wind, to be sure, but stronger than usual. And in the sky, that familiar fissure had opened up — right over an unfamiliar stretch of grassland between Big Sister’s village and the town where Éclair’s parents lived.
“So it begins…”

Once transported, I looked around and felt a faint pang of loneliness at being sent alone. Come to think of it, I’d never once experienced a wave transport without any companions at my side. It was a touch lonely, I must admit.

Ah… Father, and Filo-tan above all, and Filolial-sama… I missed Yuki-chan and the others terribly. Would this feeling lift once I got past this wave? In any case… this was the moment of truth! With that, I took a moment to survey the state of the village.
“Oh my… it really did happen.”

Older Sister stood beside Big Sister’s parents, staring at the wave with a stunned expression, harpoon gripped tight in her hands. Had this finally convinced her? Pondering that, I hurried toward the town. Monsters were pouring out in droves, a direct effect of the wave. In previous loops I’d only ever seen the corpses of these monsters — never witnessed them alive and moving.

The monsters that appeared were Dimension Skeletons, I say. In great numbers — truly, an overwhelming amount. Countless. And behind them, a Dimension Cerberus. I recognized this one too, having once examined its remains brought back to the castle — a massive dog-type monster with three heads.
“GRAAAAAAAAAAAAH!! AWOOOOOOOOOOON!”
In my usaunny form, I dashed toward the neighboring town with my swift feet. There I spotted Éclair’s parent and Crocodile Guy’s parent frantically trying to evacuate the townsfolk.
“Everyone! Evacuate calmly! We will hold the line here!”
So it seemed — they were standing at the front lines, trying to stem the tide of Dimension Skeletons and the other monsters assaulting the town.
“Shion! Guide the people to safety!”
“A-Alright!”

Crocodile Guy, under orders, was guiding the non-combatants while also finishing off stray Dimension Skeletons. A bit shaky, admittedly. And then — thud, thud — a Dimension Cerberus came charging in. Wait, hadn’t I seen a boss-type monster back at the village too? Hold on a moment. Were there multiple Dimension Cerberuses!?
“HAAAAAAAAAAAH!”

Crocodile Guy’s parent, joining forces with Éclair’s parent, fought together to draw its attention. There did seem to be quite a few capable fighters present, but they were clearly struggling. Had it not been for my and Older Sister’s behind-the-scenes maneuvering, this many capable hands likely wouldn’t have been secured, and the fight would be going far worse.
Now then — in my current form, given how many demi-humans and beastmen populated Éclair’s town, I figured I could fight without drawing too much suspicion. And so, without further ado — charge!
“Nyoink!”
“Wh-what!?”
I dashed over to the Dimension Cerberus with my swift feet and, careful not to arouse too much suspicion, swung my spear like a blunt staff and struck it.
“GRAAAH—!? YIPE!”
Thwack! My spear’s shaft landed a solid blow right on the Dimension Cerberus’s face. It yelped, then immediately turned its fury toward me, locking onto its new target.
“GRAAAAAH! GRAAAH!”

It breathed fire from its mouth — rather lukewarm, honestly. I positioned myself so no one stood behind me, dodged, closed the distance, and thrust. I wanted to finish it off in one go, but using a skill outright would give away that I was the “culprit” behind all this, so I had to gauge the situation carefully. Thunk! My spear landed a decent hit, but… hm?
“Now!”

The old soldier who seemed to be Crocodile Guy’s parent swung his axe with all his might at the Dimension Cerberus, whose attention was now fixed on me. Crunch — a solid hit, the axe sinking into its fur, though not deep enough to pierce through. It wasn’t that Crocodile Guy’s parent was weak, mind you — not at all.
“Gh… so strong. What kind of monster is this, appearing in a place like this.”
“So this is the monster spoken of in the prophecy of ruin — the one that appears with the waves.”

Hmm… this was something of a discovery, in a way. At least going by my own experience, the Dimension Cerberus was stronger than the Dimension Chimera of the next wave. In fact, its raw combat power might even exceed that of the Soul Eater, whose mechanics were more complex but whose fundamentals were simpler. Thinking back, the Dimension Chimera was something even our insufficiently-strengthened party back then could handle — and if the people of this world had already undergone local Class Ups, they’d likely put up a good fight against it. But if the Dimension Cerberus, from an earlier wave I’d vaguely assumed would be weaker, was already this strong… The Dimension Skeletons too, judging by the resistance they put up, felt tougher than the monsters from the next wave. Ordinary combatants would surely struggle against this. Though for Older Sister, this would be child’s play.
“Hey, you — small beastman there, Rapid-species! It’s dangerous, hurry and evacuate!”
The one who looked like Crocodile Guy’s parent and Éclair’s father ordered me to flee.
“That’s right! I don’t know what adventurer you are, but we’ll handle this one!”

There were other capable fighters around too, but… I’d been underestimated, I must say. No — more likely, they were simply mustering their courage to protect what mattered to them. The proper conduct of this world’s people, I’d say. Éclair’s parent’s charisma was likely what kept everyone’s morale up here. No wonder they wouldn’t think to rely on some unfamiliar beastman with no ties to their group.
“No need to worry, nyoink! No enemy can keep up with my speed, nyo-ink!”
I dashed about in zigzags, drawing the Dimension Cerberus’s attention. Then — a charge, nyoink! Thrust! I put my strength into it and pierced straight through its hide!
“GYAN!? GRRRRR! GRAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!”

The Dimension Cerberus howled in pain, radiating bloodlust and roaring at me. There were other monsters around too, and this wasn’t the only Dimension Cerberus. I had to finish it quickly! Careful not to say the skill name aloud, I unleashed Chaos Stab followed by Windmill X. Looking at the concept, it seemed simple enough to execute. Thud, thud, thud! I drove my spear in with full force, piercing straight through the Dimension Cerberus’s heart — its weak point.
“GYAAAAH!? GUGUUUUUGAAAAH!”
Even with its heart crushed, it kept moving stubbornly. Argh, persistent thing. And so large, too.
“Drop dead, nyoink!”
Slash! I lopped off two heads at once and thrust through the forehead of the last one.
“Grah—”
Thud! One down, I say.
“O-Oh… incredible.”
“You there! That was amazing!”
“You must be a traveling adventurer… but you saved us!”

Éclair’s parents and the others let out cries of admiration at the sight of the slain Dimension Cerberus, though they never let up their assault on the monsters still pouring in one after another. Crocodile Guy’s parent, however, seemed to be running low on stamina, breathing heavily now.
“Are you alright?”
“Haah… haah… I really don’t want to get old.”
A prolonged battle was clearly tough on an old soldier. Just then, a scream and a loud crash echoed from somewhere in the distance.
